components.description: Benefited employees have a right to reasonable accommodation of known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth and related conditions, and need not take leave where another reasonable accommodation can be provided.
eligible_parent: birth_parent

faculty_group: This parental leave policy applies to all benefited employees of the University and will run concurrently with FMLA leave, where applicable.
eligible_parent: Employees have a right to be free from discrimination in relation to pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions, including the right to reasonable accommodation to known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions.
entitlement: Employees have a right to be free from discrimination in relation to pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions, including the right to reasonable accommodation to known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, an employee is not required to take leave to accommodate pregnancy if there is another reasonable accommodation that can be provided to the known limitations related to the pregnancy of the employee.

notes: Source precedence: the AAUP agreement controls over conflicting University policies (Art. II; 17.1). The Faculty Handbook sets the faculty terms (family leave, parental leave, medical leave, sick leave). The General Counsel Parental Leave policy covers all benefited employees, faculty included, but its sick and vacation mechanics are written for employees who accrue sick leave (staff).

Documents and contents: 2018_00 HR Parental Leave policy (12 weeks unpaid for all benefited employees; sick/vacation use; personal leave after 12 weeks; pregnancy accommodation); 2018_01 AAUP agreement (9.5 stop the clock; 9.6 illness accommodation; 9.16 FMLA for up to one semester and the primary-caregiver administered load); 2018_02 Handbook 4.1.14 academic leaves without salary for professional purposes only (not a component: it cannot be used for a birth) and informal short leaves of a day or two (not coded); 2018_03 Handbook family leave (unpaid, up to one year per child); 2018_04 Handbook parental leave (FMLA restatement, semester of unpaid FMLA leave, time off with pay for pregnancy incapacity, the 9.16 workload option); 2018_07 Handbook medical leave (FMLA restatement for own or family serious health condition; one academic year of service); 2018_08 Handbook sick leave (informal; version uncertain, only capture 2019-09-16); 2018_09 Disability policy (salary continuation during the LTD waiting period; LTD; State DIP and SEPP paths).

Paths (U8): the Disability policy sets disability pay by retirement plan. The member's path coded is the 403(b) plan ('Faculty & Exempt Staff'; the agreement's 9.7 retirement plan is the 403(b)): no short-term disability; salary continuation during the six-month LTD waiting period (c13), then LTD (c14). Not coded: (a) State Employees' Pension Plan participants enrolled in the State DIP (29 Del. C. 5253(b)(1)): STD from the 31st calendar day after a 30-calendar-day elimination period, up to 182 calendar days, at 75% of base salary; LTD after 182 days at 60% or 66 2/3%; (b) SEPP participants not in the DIP (29 Del. C. 5524(b)(3)): full salary for the month of onset and three months, then full salary while sick leave lasts (or 60% less the state disability pension) to the end of the six-month LTD waiting period.

Service band (U8): c13's full-salary weeks step up with service (years 1-2: 8; 3-4: 12; 5-6: 16; 7-8: 20; 9+: full six months). A member with two completed years is in the third year: 12 weeks coded (as Purdue's 2-3-year band).

Chain, birth parent: family leave up to 1 year (c2), containing the semester of FMLA leave (c1, within c2), with the FMLA 12 workweeks (c6) and the HR 12-week parental leave (c7) alongside from the start; pregnancy-incapacity time off with pay (c3, no length) and salary continuation during the LTD waiting period (c13, 6 months, then LTD c14) unlinked; primary-caregiver administered load: full relief for one semester (c4) in lieu of partial relief (c5), in the semester of the birth or the one immediately following, unlinked to the leaves.

Chain, non-birth parent: family leave up to 1 year (c2) containing the semester of FMLA leave (c1), with FMLA (c6) and the HR parental leave (c7) alongside; primary-caregiver administered load c4 in lieu of c5, unlinked.

Not linked: the relief semester (c4/c5) is placed by the text relative to the birth ('during the semester of the birth ... or immediately following'), not relative to a leave; no link was coded between the relief and the leaves.

Documents cited but not saved: University Family and Medical Leave Policy (GC); Sick Leave Policy (GC, staff); Leave of Absence Without Pay Policy (GC); the disability insurance policies and plan documents (Disability policy: the plan document prevails); Faculty Handbook 4.1.14.9 Vacation Leave and 4.1.14.11 Emergency Involuntary Leave of Absence with Pay (listed in the Handbook navigation; not saved); the written policies on 'maternity leave' continued by agreement 17.1 (probably Handbook 4.1.14.3, which is saved); the 2013-2016 agreement cited by Handbook 4.1.14.3 (superseded by the saved 2016-2021 agreement); Faculty Workload Policy (Handbook section 4; workload, not leave); 29 Del. C. 5253 and 5524 (statute texts not saved).

Handbook 4.1.14.3 was read from the 2017-04-21 capture (2018_04); the document's version note says the 2018-10-26 capture has the same text. Handbook 4.1.14.4 is a 2016 capture (no 2017-18 capture); Handbook 4.1.14.8 is a 2019 capture, so c11 carries version_uncertain.

Leave limits: none recorded. The HR policy bars using vacation to extend parental leave beyond its 12 weeks (a limit on c7 itself); the family leave's two-year maximum is a career limit (flagged on c2).
